correctness.rationale: For complete-graph incidence B, BB^T=nI−J, hence each edge-coordinate restriction to ker B has norm sqrt((n−2)/n). Thus an intrinsic ball centered at x has radius sqrt(n/(n−2))*min_e x_e. Every prefix cut has k(n−k) crossing edges and conserved total beta_k, giving min_e x_e≤τ=min beta_k/[k(n−k)]. The explicit feasible x_e=τ+1_{e=(k,k+1)}(beta_k−k(n−k)τ) achieves equality; proper prefix conditions guarantee full-dimensional positive feasible flows. For every tight cut, y=x−τ1≥0 has zero crossing sum and therefore zero individual crossing values. The remaining edges decompose across contiguous blocks, each with positive internal prefix netflows; their relative affine dimensions are (d−1)(d−2)/2. With b=e1−en, central cuts maximize k(n−k), recovering the stated radius and center dimension. No general metric equivalence to alternate Birkhoff-face embeddings assumed.
residual_risks: Requires all beta_k strictly positive; if some vanish the affine hull and coordinate restriction norms can change.
Unit-source-sink theorem already contained in published electrical-antichain work, and must not be treated as original.

value.rationale: The all-prescribed-real-netflow complete-DAG family is a natural parametrization of network-flow polytopes. The exact optimal-radius geometry and entire space of incenters can undergo cut-controlled dimension transitions; identifying its product decomposition and dimension for every positive prefix vector gives more than a routine scalar max-min LP value.
residual_risks: Classical feasibility and effective resistance identities are ingredients rather than new results.

limitations: Relative to the published unit-flow antichain theorem, credit is limited to arbitrary b and complete tight-cut factorization; metric is edge-Euclidean only.
